summary: A quick two-player card game where players jointly build shared 'mandala' mountains of colored cards whose point values aren't fixed until later in the game, then race to claim the best-valued cards into their own river and cup. The tension comes from not knowing which colors will end up valuable until it's almost too late to react.
praised: clever hidden-value scoring twist that keeps both players guessing until late
tight, elegant two-player duel with a short playtime
high rules-to-depth ratio typical of the designers' other work
criticised: thin theme that feels attached after the fact
niche appeal mostly to fans of abstract two-player duels

interaction.detail: Both players contribute cards to the same shared mandala mountains and later choose from them in turn order, directly competing for which colors end up in their own river and cup. Most of the visible board state is shared, while each player's collected river/cup is private.

subsystems: head-to-head color majority scoring from river/cup card collections
sources: each color's collected cards, compared between players
scoring.how_you_win: As each mandala fills with all six colors, players draft cards from it into their own river and cup; once the cards run out, each color is scored by comparing who collected more of it, and the player with the higher overall total wins.
